title: Revit View Standards and Template Use
purpose: Apply governed Revit view naming, view templates, visibility/filter controls, and view-purpose settings consistently while keeping unresolved office-specific template names and example view names noncanonical.
preconditions: The project's governing view/naming rules and approved view templates are available.
Project phase and intended view purpose are known.

steps.name: Name the view for governed purpose
actions: Assign a name that identifies the view type, scope/location, discipline where applicable, and purpose using the governing naming rules.
Do not adopt source example view names as canonical unless they are present in the governed naming registry.
validation: View names are consistent, searchable, and aligned to the governing S4 naming structures.
No duplicate or ad-hoc naming convention is introduced.

steps.name: Apply the approved view template
actions: Apply the approved view template for the view's purpose and type.
Use template-controlled category visibility, filters, linked-model visibility, phase/phase filter, detail level, and visual style where governed.
If a recurring exception is required, route it into template governance instead of accumulating per-view overrides.
validation: The expected view template is applied where required.
Temporary or unexplained per-view overrides are absent or recorded as governed exceptions.

steps.name: Verify purpose-specific display state
actions: Confirm detail level and visual style match the view's intended use.
Confirm phase and phase filter align with project requirements.
Confirm linked-model visibility and filter behavior are controlled through governed view/template logic rather than ad-hoc settings.
validation: The view state is consistent with its governed purpose and template.
The view can be used for its intended documentation, coordination, or export function without undocumented graphics drift.

outputs: Governed Revit views with consistent naming and template-controlled graphics
evidence: View schedule or API inventory of names and applied templates
future_dependencies: Complete view-purpose vocabulary where not already governed
governance_notes: Exact source-era view-template names and example view names are TODO/example content and are not promoted.
Category-level graphics authority remains with governed Object Styles/graphics structures; views implement scoped display behavior.

provenance.migration_note: Normalized as L6 view implementation guidance; generic/example view names and unresolved template names remain noncanonical.
